cards.claim: NCERT Class XI Chemistry Unit 1 expects learners to understand the role of chemistry in different spheres of life, explain the characteristics of the three states of matter, and classify substances into elements, compounds and mixtures.
cards.quote: understand the role of chemistry in different spheres of life; • explain the characteristics of three states of matter; • classify different substances into elements, compounds and mixtures;

cards.claim: Matter is anything that has mass and occupies space.
cards.quote: Anything which has mass and occupies space is called matter.

cards.claim: A pure substance has constituent particles all of the same chemical nature; a mixture contains particles of two or more pure substances in any ratio, so its composition is variable.
cards.quote: When all constituent particles of a substance are same in chemical nature, it is said to be a pure substance. A mixture contains many types of particles. a mixture contains parti cles of two or more pure substances which may be present in it in any ratio. Hence, their composition is variable.

cards.claim: Solids have definite volume and definite shape; liquids have definite volume but no definite shape and take the shape of their container.
cards.quote: (i) Solids have definite volume and definite shape. (ii) Liquids have definite volume but do not have definite shape. They take the shape of the container in which they are placed.

cards.claim: The three states of matter are interconvertible, but only by changing the conditions of temperature and pressure.
cards.quote: These three states of matter are interconvertible by changing the conditions of temperature and pressure.

cards.claim: NCERT example of a pure substance: glucose contains carbon, hydrogen and oxygen in a fixed ratio, with particles of the same composition, so it has a fixed composition.
cards.quote: Glucose contains carbon, hydrogen and oxygen in a fixed ratio and its particles are of same composition. Hence, like all other pure substances, glucose has a fixed composition.

cards.claim: A compound does not keep the properties of its elements: hydrogen and oxygen are gases, but water, the compound they form, is a liquid.
cards.quote: Also, the properties of a compound are different from those of its constituent elements. For example, hydrogen and oxygen are gases, whereas, the compound formed by their combination i.e., water is a liquid.

cards.claim: NCERT Exemplar (Chemistry XI) 1.12 (MCQ I): which statement about a compound is incorrect: atoms of different elements; not separable by physical methods; retains physical properties of its elements; fixed ratio of atoms?
cards.quote: Which of the following statements about a compound is incorrect? (i) A molecule of a compound has atoms of different elements. (ii) A compound cannot be separated into its constituent elements by physical methods of separation. (iii) A compound retains the physical properties of its constituent elements. (iv) The ratio of atoms of different elements in a compound is fixed.

cards.claim: Prerequisite-level official question (NCERT Exemplar Science Class IX, ch. 2, MCQ 8): for 2A + B -> A2B, which statements are incorrect (A2B shows properties of A and B; fixed composition; not a compound; an element)?
cards.quote: Two substances, A and B were made to react to form a third substance, A2B according to the following reaction 2 A + B → A2 B Which of the following statements concerning this reaction are incorrect? (i) The product A2B shows the properties of substances A and B (ii) The product will always have a fixed composition (iii) The product so formed cannot be classified as a compound (iv) The product so formed is an element (a) (i), (ii) and (iii), (b) (ii), (iii) and (iv) (c) (i), (iii) and (iv) (d) (ii), (iii) and (iv)
